items.stem: In a mathematics test, Amina scores 34 out of 40.

parts.t: Write Amina’s mark as a percentage.

Bilal scores 65% in the same test.
Work out Bilal’s mark.

sols: write the score as a fraction of the total, then multiply by 100

items.stem:
A jacket has a normal price of $80.
In a sale, the price of the jacket is reduced by 15%.

parts.t: Work out the sale price of the jacket.

sols: Alternative: the sale price is 100 − 15 = 85% of $80, so 0.85 × 80 = $68

items.stem:
Rashid buys a car for $12 500.
Three years later he sells the car for $9750.

parts.t: Calculate the percentage loss.

sols: the percentage change is always compared with the original amount

items.stem:
The price of a mobile phone is increased by 20%.
The new price is $432.

parts.t: Calculate the price of the phone before the increase.

sols: After a 20% increase the new price is 120% of the original price.
120% of the original price = 432, so 1.2 × original = 432
the multiplier for a 20% increase is 1.2
divide by the multiplier — do not take 20% off $432
ms:
M1 for 432 associated with 120% oe
M1 for 432 ÷ 1.2 oe
A1
cao; 345.6 scores 0

items.stem:
There are 960 students in a school.
55% of these students are boys.

parts.t: Work out the number of girls in the school.

25% of the girls play hockey.
Work out the number of girls who play hockey.

sols: the two percentages must add up to 100%
25% is the same as one quarter

items.stem: Nadia invests $2400 in an account paying 3.5% per year compound interest.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of her investment at the end of 4 years.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Work out the total interest she earns in these 4 years.

sols: The multiplier for one year is 1 + <sup>3.5</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> = 1.035.
each year the money is 103.5% of the amount at the start of that year
ms:
M1 for 1.035 seen as a multiplier
M1 for 2400 × 1.0354 oe
A1
accept 2754.055… ; 2754 alone scores M2A0

items.stem:
In a sale, the price of a laptop is reduced by 12%.
The sale price of the laptop is $528.

parts.t: Calculate the price of the laptop before the sale.

After the sale, the shop increases the sale price of $528 by 12%.
Work out this new price.

sols: A 12% reduction leaves 100 − 12 = 88% of the original price.
0.88 is the multiplier for a 12% decrease
increasing by 12% does not undo a 12% decrease, because the 12% is now taken of a smaller amount
ms:
M1 for 528 associated with 88% oe
M1 for 528 ÷ 0.88 oe
A1
cao; 591.36 scores 0

items.stem:
A van is bought for $24 000.
Its value depreciates by 18% of its value at the start of each year.

parts.t:
Calculate the value of the van at the end of 3 years.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate the overall percentage decrease in the value of the van over these 3 years.

sols: Each year the van keeps 100 − 18 = 82% of its value, so the multiplier is 0.82.
exact value $13 232.83 to the nearest cent
Overall multiplier = 0.82<sup>3</sup> = 0.551368, so the value left is 55.1368% of the original.
not 3 × 18 = 54%, because each 18% is of a smaller amount
ms:
M1 for 0.82 seen as a multiplier
M1 for 24000 × 0.823 oe
A1
accept 13232.8… or 13232.83

items.stem:
A shopkeeper buys 120 shirts at $14 each.
She sells 90 of the shirts at a profit of 45% each.
She sells the remaining shirts at cost price.

parts.t: Work out the selling price of one of the 90 shirts.
Calculate the total amount of money she receives for all 120 shirts.
Calculate her percentage profit on the 120 shirts.

sols: a 45% profit means the multiplier is 1.45
compare the profit with the total cost price

items.stem:
Mrs Osei buys a house for $180 000.
In the first year the value of the house increases by 6%.
In the second year the value increases by a further 4%.

parts.t: Calculate the value of the house at the end of the second year.
Calculate the overall percentage increase in the value of the house over the two years.

During the third year the value falls, so that at the end of the third year the house is worth $180 000 again.
Calculate the percentage decrease in the third year.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: not 6 + 4 = 10%, because the 4% is taken of the larger amount
the decrease is compared with the value at the start of the third year

parts.t: Write <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> as a percentage.
Work out 12.5% of 640.

sols: convert the fraction to a decimal
multiply by 100 to change a decimal into a percentage

items.stem: 15% of a number is 42.

parts.t: Find the number.

sols: 15% of the number = 42, so 1% of the number = 42 ÷ 15 = 2.8

items.stem:
A bottle contains 1.5 litres of water.
Yara drinks 450 millilitres of the water.

parts.t: Work out the percentage of the water that Yara drinks.
Write down the percentage of the water that is left in the bottle.

sols: both quantities must be in the same units before comparing

items.stem:
Ten years ago the population of Oakford was 2400.
The population of Oakford is now 2790.

parts.t: Calculate the percentage increase in the population of Oakford.

Ten years ago the population of Ashwell was 1850.
It has increased by 12%.
Work out the population of Ashwell now.

sols: compare the increase with the original population

items.stem: Karim invests $3500 in an account paying 2.4% per year simple interest.

parts.t: Calculate the interest Karim receives after 5 years.
Work out the total amount in the account after 5 years.

sols: simple interest is the same every year, always on the original $3500

items.stem:
The marked price of a bicycle is $640.
In a sale the marked price is reduced by 25%.
Sales tax of 8% is then added to the sale price.

parts.t: Work out the sale price before tax.
Calculate the price paid, including sales tax.
Calculate the overall percentage change from the marked price to the price paid.

sols: so the price paid is 81% of the marked price

items.stem:
1200 people watch a concert.
60% of the people are adults.
35% of the adults are members of the concert club.

parts.t: Work out the number of adults.
Work out the number of adults who are members of the concert club.
Calculate the percentage of the 1200 people who are adult members of the concert club.

sols: the 35% is a percentage of the adults, not of everybody
a percentage of a percentage is found by multiplying

items.stem:
Leila invests a sum of money at 4% per year compound interest.
At the end of 2 years the investment is worth $4326.40.

parts.t: Calculate the sum of money Leila invested.
Work out the total interest earned in the 2 years.

sols: Each year multiplies the money by 1.04, so after 2 years the multiplier is 1.04<sup>2</sup> = 1.0816.
compound interest: interest is added each year
divide by the multiplier to reverse the growth
ms:
M1 for 1.042 or 1.0816 seen
M1 for 4326.40 ÷ 1.042 oe
A1
cao

items.stem:
Farah has $5000 to invest for 3 years. She has two choices.

Bank A: 3.2% per year simple interest.
Bank B: 3% per year compound interest.

parts.t: Calculate the value of the investment after 3 years with Bank A.

Calculate the value of the investment after 3 years with Bank B.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
Which bank gives Farah more money after 3 years, and by how much?

sols: over a short period a slightly higher simple rate can beat a lower compound rate
ms:
B1
FT their (a) − their (b), correct bank named

items.stem:
Marco earns $28 000 in a year.
The first $12 000 of his earnings is not taxed.
He pays income tax at 20% on the rest of his earnings.

parts.t: Calculate the income tax Marco pays in the year.

Calculate the income tax as a percentage of his total earnings.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: tax is only charged on the amount above the tax-free allowance
compare the tax with the whole $28 000, not the taxable part
less than 20% because part of the earnings is untaxed

items.stem:
The price of a table is $250.
The price is increased by 20%.
One month later the new price is decreased by 20%.

parts.t: Calculate the final price of the table.

Hassan says “the final price is the same as the original price”.
Explain why Hassan is wrong, and find the overall percentage change in the price.

sols: the 20% decrease is 20% of $300, which is $60, not $50
the 20% off is taken from a larger amount than the 20% added
ms:
B1
e.g. 20% of 300 is 60 not 50, or 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96; FT their (a)

items.stem:
Pack A of rice has a mass of 500 g and costs $3.60.
Pack B has 20% more rice than Pack A and costs 15% more than Pack A.

parts.t: Work out the mass of rice in Pack B and the cost of Pack B.

Which pack is better value for money?
Show your working.

sols: Pack B is better value, because 69 cents per 100 g is less than 72 cents per 100 g.
the mass rose by a larger percentage than the price
ms:
M1 for a comparable rate for both packs, e.g. 0.72 and 0.69 per 100 g, or 138.9 g and 144.9 g per dollar
A1 Pack B with correct figures; FT their (a)

items.stem:
Dana invests $6000 at a rate of r% per year compound interest.
At the end of 2 years the investment is worth $6741.60.

parts.t: Find the value of r.
Find the number of complete years after which the investment is first worth more than $8000.

sols: take the square root; the multiplier must be positive
So the investment is first worth more than $8000 after 5 years.
trial with whole numbers of years
ms:
M1 for 6000 × 1.064 (= 7574.86) or 6000 × 1.065 (= 8029.35) seen, or a correct use of logarithms
A1
FT their r

items.stem:
The value of a motorbike decreases by 15% each year.
At the end of 3 years the motorbike is worth $9826.

parts.t: Calculate the value of the motorbike when it was new.
Find the number of complete years after which the motorbike is first worth less than half of its value when new.

sols: Each year the motorbike keeps 85% of its value, so the multiplier is 0.85 and after 3 years it is 0.85<sup>3</sup> = 0.614125.
divide by the multiplier to reverse the depreciation
The value is less than half when 0.85n < 0.5.
the original value cancels, so no need to use $16 000
So it is first worth less than half after 5 years.
ms:
M1 for 0.853 or 0.614125 seen
M1 for 9826 ÷ 0.853 oe
A1
cao

M1 for 0.854 (= 0.522…) or 0.855 (= 0.444…) seen, or their 8000 compared with 16000 × 0.85n
A1

items.stem:
Yusuf buys 250 kg of mangoes at $1.80 per kilogram.
8% of the mangoes are damaged and are thrown away.
He sells all the remaining mangoes at $2.75 per kilogram.

parts.t: Work out the mass of mangoes that Yusuf sells.

Calculate his percentage profit.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Yusuf wants to make a profit of exactly 50%.
Calculate the price per kilogram at which he must sell the remaining mangoes.
Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.

sols: he pays for all 250 kg, including the damaged ones
profit compared with the cost price
For a 50% profit the money received must be 1.5 × 450 = $675
the $675 must come from the 230 kg he actually sells
to the nearest cent (2.93 would give slightly less than 50%)
ms:
M1 for 1.5 × 450 (= 675) ÷ their 230
A1
accept 2.93 only if 2.934… seen
